title: The Stolen Creek of Dry Willow
moral: True courage is steady and standing up for what is right, even when it is difficult.

story: Luke Mercer, a young cowboy, discovers that Dry Willow Creek is nearly dry and meets Aiyana, who explains that the water has been diverted by a powerful rancher named Hargrove. She gives Luke an agreement proving her people’s right to the water and asks him to take it to Red Mesa. Luke investigates and finds a trench redirecting the creek, but he is confronted and threatened by Hargrove’s men. Determined to help, Luke rides through the night, escaping a dangerous chase, and reaches Red Mesa where he convinces the commissioner and Deputy Sloane to act. Together, they return to the creek and confront Hargrove. With courage, Luke removes the stones blocking the water, allowing it to flow back to its rightful path. The law is enforced, and the creek is restored. In the end, Luke learns that true courage is not loud but steady, and that perseverance and doing what is right can bring justice.
